renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror: true/untrue, little/much, eternal/non-eternal, Māyā-stained/self-pure. That all, from own-grasping-consciousness-rise, form-light-natured, having known — own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship. Knowing that all opposites shine in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness = glory = Lordhood; its last word is the imperative it opened with the stance for.

paragraphs.text: Everything opposite shines in one place: the mirror of consciousness. True things and untrue things. Little things and big things. What lasts and what does not. What is stained by illusion and what is pure by itself. Now know this: all of that rises from your own grasping consciousness, is made of form-and-light, and knowing it turns into glory that rises out of your own experience. That glory is Lordhood itself — so worship.
Knowing that every opposite shines in the mirror from your own grasping = glory = Lordhood. The last word is the same as the first stance: worship.
